## Natural history notes

A small crambid moth characterized by narrow tan to brownish wings with subtle darker lines, patches, or mottled markings typical of many grass moth relatives. In Florida, it has been recorded as part of the North American range, but its specific larval host plants and habitat associations appear to be poorly documented. Adults are likely nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars probably feed concealed on plant material, as is common for related crambid moths, and serve as prey for spiders, birds, bats, and other insect-eating animals.
